parts.title: Part 3 · Gap fill
parts.instr: Write ONE word in each gap.

items.q: I don’t like being dependent ____ you for money; I want to work.
The standard of living in the eastern region of the country is, on the ____ , higher than elsewhere.
Robert seems irritated today. I ____ why. Shall I ask what’s wrong?
There’s a smell coming from our fridge. Something has ____ bad in there!
Don’t let me ____ ; I’m depending on your help.
The starter and main course were tasty. Then, to ____ , Sarah served us her famous banana ice cream!
Could you possibly lay the ____ for dinner? You know where everything is.
I’m going to marry Lisa; ____ is, if she says yes!
A strong coffee each morning is fine, but it is not wise ____ throughout the day as if it were water.
The team always do physical exercise first ____ in the morning.
We’d better inform the police about the gun we found in the garden, ____ we?
The four brothers didn’t get ____ well, and violence was common.
I commanded the men ____ the building.
Is it true that eating oranges helps to guard ____ colds?
Do you think telling jokes is a good way to ____ the ice at dinner parties?

parts.title: Part 5 · Error correction
parts.instr: Correct the mistake in each sentence. You can add one word, take out one word, or change one word. Type the whole corrected sentence.

items.text: Nothing I do is a waste my time; I plan carefully and fill every minute of my day.
Before entering the castle, my colleague Sandra and I are going to divide you all among two groups.
I have the taste for simple but healthy food, and I spend very little time cooking in the kitchen.
When I lived in southern Spain as a child, I was use to hot weather, but I’m not now.
Marisa shouldn’t spoken to her father like that yesterday; it was rude.
I wanted to get a car but didn’t buy anything at the end. I don’t really need one.
Bob hates the food here in Spain, and he doesn’t like the weather too.
I’m afraid I can’t talk to you right moment. Can I call you back in five minutes?
That was a long run. You can be tired now!
I wish we knew more about this neighbourhood before moving here.

parts.text: The expression “quite a few” means “a fairly large number of”. A snag is a small problem. A seat is anything that we sit on. By a dull person, we mean a boring person. The words “or so” mean “about”. We recycle waste paper, or throw it away. The three forms of “light” are “light, lit, lit”. The three forms of “quit” are “quit, quit, quit”. Remember to vote in the election next week. I’m afraid I can’t talk to you right now. The twins are so similar that I sometimes mistake one for the other. Don’t let me down; I’m depending on your help.
